documents.unit: Academic Senate, Ad hoc Subcommittee on AI
documents.title: Ad hoc Subcommittee on Artificial Intelligence (AI) Running Report, Winter 2024
tiers: permit on conditions, undergraduate (sample syllabus statement)
permit on conditions, graduate (sample syllabus statement)
documents.summary: A Senate subcommittee report that gathers recommendations from campus partners (privacy, IT, HR, admissions, libraries, advising) and proposes two sample syllabus statements, one banning AI and one permitting it on conditions. It sets no university-wide rule on student AI use and leaves the choice to each instructor.
documents.stance_why: The report sets no university-wide rule: "the inclusion of such statements is the instructor's decision" and "faculty need to decide whether AI can be used as a supplement, teaching, or support tool". It offers a prohibit template and permit templates for undergraduate and graduate courses, so the stance is delegates with tiers.

units.fit_note: The reluctance is the committee's own and is tied to privacy breaches; it is not addressed to students.

documents.title: Student Code of Conduct revision resolution (Section 2.3 Cheating includes AI)
documents.summary: A Senate resolution revising the Student Code of Conduct so that cheating includes using AI tools in coursework unless the instructor authorized it in advance and the use is cited. It binds all students and passed unanimously.
documents.stance_why: Section 2.3 defines cheating to include using AI tools "in academic coursework, except where such use has been authorized in advance by the instructor and disclosed", so AI is banned unless explicitly permitted, which is restrict.
